planning.storytellingVoice: Intimate character drama: quiet longing and the difference between being seen and admitting distress.
planning.desire: Keep himself occupied and avoid a lonely evening.
planning.obstacle: Hannah is missing; Connie is unreliable; the school day ends.
planning.earlyCare: A teenager longs for a dependable adult but is embarrassed to need help.
planning.payoff: After being seen by Jeremy, Alden finds that Gorgon is still there.
planning.continuingQuestion: What can Alden and Gorgon say to each other when everyone else has gone?
planning.direction: Shared framing for Jeremy’s question, Alden listener shot for being seen, then shared reply. Final two-shot makes company visible; no invented dialogue from Gorgon.

signatures.Alden: Self-correcting, private vulnerability; lowered gaze and restrained expressions.
signatures.Gorgon: Silent presence only in this source boundary.

opening.style: Charcoal with muted ochre and blue soft pastel on textured paper
opening.moment: Alden tells Jeremy he is okay while concealing his sadness.
opening.speaker: Alden

continuation.end: Alden recognizes how much Hannah mattered to him, reassures Jeremy without sharing his grief, and stays for writing class to avoid a lonely home. When everyone leaves he returns to Gorgon’s desk.
continuation.nextStart: “Do you have a room to sleep in? When everybody leaves?”
continuation.note: Alden asks about Gorgon’s living conditions and loneliness. Gorgon describes his unwanted celebrity; Alden recognizes the cruelty of being unable to escape cameras. Stop before Alden manages his pity and proposes crickets.
